title: Surgical evacuation runbook and opaque-state telemetry for active-passive promotion
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Purpose: Build a precise ("surgical") active->passive evacuation runbook that minimizes customer-visible impact by combining targeted circuit-breaker triggers, priority-aware load shedding, and an opaque-state telemetry layer that surfaces state divergence without exposing PII. Background: Recent tabletop exercises highlighted two gaps: (1) lack of granular state-diff signals during promotion, and (2) repairs often required manual reconciliation after restores. This ticket scopes a runbook, an opaque telemetry schema (fingerprints + invariant checks), and an automated restore-validation harness to run as part of scheduled failover drills. Goals: (a) a documented play that on-call can execute in <= 20 minutes to promote standby region and rehydrate critical state; (b) telemetry that flags divergence >0.5% on critical keyspace and exports reconciler actions; (c) a post-switchover verification job that asserts KV checksums and a sample replay for top N customers. Success metrics: drill completion time, percent of checks passing, and mean customer error-rate delta during promotion.
checklist: Define opaque-state telemetry schema: fingerprint, invariant tags, sample hashes
Integrate telemetry into tokenstore and routing layer with low overhead (<1% CPU)
Author step-by-step evacuation runbook with operator commands and automated sanity checks
Wire circuit-breaker thresholds into evacuation sequence (soft-fence -> hard cutover)
Implement restore-verification harness: checksums, top-200 replay, data drift scorer
Create Canary drill job in CI to validate the whole flow against test fixtures
Run two dry-run drills: internal staging and small-customer simulation
Collect telemetry, iterate thresholds, add dashboard widgets and runbook links
notes: 2026-02-20: Scoping meeting with PM/Oncall. Agreed to focus on tokenstore + routing state first. Luca to own runbook steps; Aisha to land telemetry schema.
2026-02-25: Decision: use compact fingerprint (xxhash64) + invariant labels to avoid PII; accepted trade-off of losing per-key debug for higher privacy and speed.
2026-03-01: Prototype telemetry landed in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/evac-telemetry (PR DRAFT). Early perf shows ~0.6% CPU, need micro-optimizations.
2026-03-03: Circuit-breaker design review with SRE: we will adopt a two-stage soft-fence (throttled routing + slow-path reads) then hard fence (fail-fast) with hysteresis window 90s.

2026-03-06: Dry-run 1 (staging): promotion sequence executed under synthetic load. Observed 7% spike in tail latency during replay; mitigations: staggered replay and small batch size for top-200 users.
2026-03-08: Review feedback from Security: telemetry exposures validated against privacy checklist. Added encryption-at-rest for trace blobs and redaction filter for debug dumps.

2026-03-10: Dry-run 2 (canary customers): runbook executed by oncall with PR checklist. Restore-verification harness detected 0.8% drift in auxiliary indices — created follow-up ENG-208101 to tighten snapshot cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can execute the runbook end-to-end in <= 20 minutes and follow build-in checks
Opaque-state telemetry visualized on dashboard with alerting for divergence > 0.5%
Restore-verification harness passes in CI (checksums + sample replay) for two consecutive runs
Circuit-breaker and load-shedding steps in runbook automatically adjust routing within SLOs (latency and error budgets)
Drill postmortem produced with clear action items and at most 3 follow-up tickets
